risks.risk: Exact camera model is not readable; pricing varies a lot by Nikon DSLR model (e.g., D3xxx vs D7xxx).
risks.proof: Ask for a photo of the camera model name/number on the body (or the 'About/Model' screen) plus the lens mount area clearly.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a generic Nikon DSLR kit with two lenses at the lower end of the matching comparables.

risks.risk: Lens focal lengths may not be exactly 18-55mm + 50mm (could be different primes/zooms).
risks.proof: Ask for close-up photos of both lenses showing the printed focal length (e.g., '18-55mm' and '50mm') and lens mount markings.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not-confirmed lens set (worst case: treat as only a typical kit zoom value).

risks.risk: Shutter count claim may be false or unverified; high shutter wear reduces value.
risks.proof: Ask for a screenshot/photo from the camera or a shutter-count app showing the shutter count.
risks.if_unproven: Price as higher-wear DSLR (worst case within the comparable range).

risks.risk: Lens condition (fungus/scratches/haze) can’t be confirmed from this single wide shot.
risks.proof: Ask for macro close-ups of both lenses front glass and rear glass against a bright light, plus a photo of the lens elements at an angle.
risks.if_unproven: Price as if lens condition is unknown (worst case: assume possible minor issues).

risks.risk: Functionality (autofocus, image stabilization, video, buttons) not tested in photos.
risks.proof: Ask for a short video clip sample (handheld) showing autofocus and recording, and a photo of the rear screen playback.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not fully proven for video/AF (worst case: assume basic functionality only).

proof_requests: Photo showing the exact Nikon DSLR model (e.g., D3300/D3400/D90/D7200 etc.)—either on the body or in the camera 'About' screen.
Close-up photos of both lenses with printed focal lengths clearly visible (18-55mm and 50mm) and lens front/rear glass under light.
Screenshot/photo of shutter count from the camera/app.
Photo of the battery and charger labels (to confirm originality) and a quick test video clip showing autofocus + recording.
response.reason: The photo confirms a Nikon DSLR with two lenses, but the exact camera model and lens focal lengths (which determine the correct comparable price) are not readable, and key claims like shutter count and lens condition are not verifiable from the single image.
